AbandonArgs.description: `abandon`: removes changes from active state; descendants are re-parented.

ArchiveArgs.description:
`archive`: metadata for the streamed payload; bytes ride `Stdout`

ArchiveFormat.description: The archive payloads the daemon streams.

AttestAddArgs.description:
`attest.add`: the signature is over [`AttestStatement::canonical_payload_v2`]
in namespace `ruk-attest`; private keys never reach the coordinator.
Statements without evidence signed over
[`AttestStatement::canonical_payload_v1`] stay verifiable.

AttestKind.description: Attestation kind: non-empty UTF-8 with no control characters, at most one control frame (16777216 bytes).

AttestListArgs.description:
`attest.list`.

`kind` selects one exact kind; `kind_prefix` selects every kind starting
with the prefix, for CI dashboards scanning `ci/` verdicts. Both set
filters combine: a statement matches when its kind equals `kind` and
starts with `kind_prefix`.

kind_prefix.description:
Only kinds starting with this prefix. Appended last so the postcard
encoding of every earlier field is unchanged; the field is optional,
so older JSON without it decodes to no prefix filter.

AttestRequirement.description: An attestation the land policy requires before execution.

valid_until.description:
The latest `signed_at` this requirement accepts; absent never
expires. A later-signed match reports `Gap::Expired`.

AttestResult.description: Attestation result: non-empty UTF-8 with no control characters, at most one control frame (16777216 bytes).

AttestSignature.description: Armored SSH signature (namespace `ruk-attest`, ed25519), at most 8192 bytes.

AttestStatement.description:
What a signer attests about one exact object.

`evidence` is appended last so the postcard encoding of every earlier
field is unchanged; stored v1 rows decode through the versioned fallback
in `attestation::rows`.

evidence.description:
The SHA-256 of an external blob this statement binds, such as a CI
log. `None` and `Some(zero)` differ on the wire: absence encodes as an
empty field, presence as exactly 32 bytes.

signed_at.description: A claim, never an ordering authority.

supersedes.description: The earlier statement this one explicitly supersedes.

AttestationStatus.description: Whether a verified statement currently counts.

oneOf.description: The same signer has conflicting live results for the same kind.

BookmarkResolution.description: The decision that resolves a conflicted native bookmark.

BookmarkResolveArgs.description:
`bookmark.resolve`: `expected_terms` are the conflict terms the caller
saw; the resolution publishes a ref and removes the conflict atomically.

BookmarkSetArgs.description:
`bookmark.set`: `name` is a full `refs/heads/` ref name. `expected` is the
old value the update is conditional on (`Absent` to create); an
unconditional `Any` is refused.

BookmarkTarget.description: What a bookmark points at. A conflicted head cannot become a Git ref.

ByteSource.description:
Where a read reply's bytes are: in the frame, or on a stream.
Producers must use `Streamed` for any body that would push the
reply past [`MAX_CONTROL_FRAME_BYTES`]; the transport layer writes
exactly `size` bytes on `stream` after the reply frame, and the
caller correlates them by stream id. No served read produces one
yet: every served page fits the control bound with room to spare,
and the first bulk-body producer owns the delivery half.

ByteString.description: Exact bytes: a JSON string when valid UTF-8, else {"hex": lowercase hex}.

Capabilities.description: The capability set of a session or the policy ceiling of a principal.

attest.description:
Attestation kinds this session may record. A grant ending in `/`
is a namespace prefix (for example `ci/` covers `ci/build`); any
other grant matches exactly, so `ci` never covers `ci/build`.

claim_paths.description: Path subtrees this session may claim.

land.description: Target refs this session may land into.

push_refs.description: Remote refs this session may push.

ChangeHead.description: A change and the exact head it resolved to.

ChangeId.description: Change identity: 16 bytes as 32 reverse-hex characters (nibble 0 = z ... nibble 15 = k).

ChangeRef.description:
A native change, optionally pinned to one of its heads. With a head, the
head is an expectation (it must still be a current head of the change) and
the way to choose among divergent heads. Without one, the change must have
exactly one current head or the call fails `E_DIVERGENT`.

ClaimAcquireArgs.description: `claim.acquire`: each path claims itself and everything below it.

subject.description:
Task/change subject for task-keyed claims; absent for path-only
claims. Only subject-carrying acquisitions may use task-lease
lifetimes above [`MAX_CLAIM_TTL_SECONDS`].

oneOf.description: This session's claims.
Every session's claims; needs `read_intents.claims`.

ClaimMode.description: Whether an overlapping write fails or only warns.

oneOf.description: Overlapping writes by other sessions fail `E_CLAIMED`.
Overlapping writes succeed with a warning.

on_behalf_of.description:
Provenance the acquiring invocation declared; never an
authorization input.

subject.description:
Task/change subject for task-keyed claims; absent for path-only
claims. Renewals preserve it; releases and sweeps drop the record
with it.

ClaimRenewArgs.description: `claim.renew`: extends one held claim by a fresh lifetime.

ClaimSubject.description:
What a claim is held for: the task/change subject key alongside paths.

A task-keyed claim carries `task:<id>` so one record covers the intent's
declared paths across rukie restarts; a change-keyed claim names the Ruk
change under review. Path-only claims carry no subject and stay capped
at [`MAX_CLAIM_TTL_SECONDS`].

oneOf.description: A rukie task (intent); the subject key renders as `task:<id>`.
The Ruk change under review; the subject key is the change id.

ClaimTtl.description: Claim lifetime in seconds, at most one day for task-keyed claims.

CommitKey.description:
Native identity of a conflicted commit record.

The key is the repository-kind hash of the exact framed record bytes
`conflict-v1 <decimal payload length>\0<payload>` (see
`conflict::ConflictRecord::key`). It therefore has the same width as the
repository's [`Oid`]s, and the `conflict-v1` framing keeps it in a
separate domain from every Git object id: a Git object header begins
`blob `, `tree `, `commit ` or `tag `, never `conflict-v1 `.

CommitRecord.description: The serialized form: metadata plus canonical bytes.

CommitRev.description:
A revision naming one commit: either a ref resolved at read time or a
literal object id. Reads that accept revisions (tree, compare, archive,
blame) take this shape instead of free-form strings.

CompareArgs.description: `compare`: merge bases plus bounded ahead/behind counts.

exact.description: False when the walk exhausted its budget: counts are lower bounds.

ConeDirs.description:
The directories a cone-mode scope lists, canonical: sorted bytewise, no
duplicates, and none below another (`a` already covers `a/b`).

Built through [`Scope::cone`]; deserialization canonicalizes, because a
redundant spelling means the same scope. A directory is never the empty
path: the root's files are always in scope.

Content.description: Content to write: inline when small, staged when large.

workspaces.description:
Workspaces whose checked-out change may be rewritten, with the stamps
the caller expects.

DiffBlob.description: One side of a file diff.

DriverDecision.description: A recorded driver decision for one path.

EditAction.description: What one explicit edit does to its path.

oneOf.description: Create or replace a file with this content.
Create or replace a symbolic link.
Remove the file or link at this path.

EditArgs.description: `edit`: checks a change out into a workspace.

EffectiveIdentity.description: The exact identity an operation recorded, and why.

Encoded.description: The canonical bytes a record is stored and transferred as.

oneOf.description: A Git commit payload.
A framed `conflict-v1` record.

ErrorCode.description:
The one closed error-code registry. The serde and schema form is the
contract spelling (`E_STALE`), identical to [`ErrorCode::as_str`].

ErrorDetail.description: Structured data attached to an error whose outcome the caller needs.

oneOf.description: A rejected or uncertain push: the durable plan and per-ref outcomes.

An HTTP failure with the facts a caller needs to classify it: the
status, the `Retry-After` delay when the server sent one, the
redirect target for 3xx, and a scrubbed body preview capped at 512
bytes. Appended after `Push`, so existing encodings are unchanged.

A detail this build does not model: tolerated so newer writers do
not break older readers. Never constructed locally.

ErrorReply.description:
The error body of a failed request. Callers branch on `code`.

The daemon's IPC `Error` frame carries this body. The trailing fields
default so a payload written before they existed still decodes.

EventSource.description:
What published one batch of ref mutations: the lane, the receive-pack
path, a local command, or a lifecycle importer. Recorded on every ref
event; never an authorization input.

EventsTailArgs.description:
`events.tail`: ref events strictly after `after`, long-polled. The
only ref feed.

prefix.description: Only events whose ref name starts with these bytes.

expired.description:
True when `after + 1` predates `oldest`: the caller missed events
and must resnapshot from `refs.list` with `as_of`.

head.description: The last assigned sequence at reply time.

oldest.description: The oldest retained sequence at reply time.

FetchArgs.description:
`fetch`: stages verified objects, then publishes the requested ref and
tracking deltas atomically.

oneOf.description: Omit blobs (`blob:none`); the native default.

FetchRefs.description: Which remote refs a fetch brings in.

shallow.description: The store now has shallow boundaries.

FileArgs.description: `file`: a file, link, gitlink, directory listing, or conflict at a path.

path.description: The path to read; absent is the root directory.

oneOf.description:
The path is conflicted; the terms are the original algebra, not a
marker rendering.

FileTerm.description: One side of a conflicted file.

Fix.description:
A machine-readable remedy attached to an error. Callers act on these, never
on message text.

oneOf.description:
Re-read the state and retry with fresh expected stamps and a new
request id.
Take the workspace (advancing its lease epoch) before mutating it.
The request id was used with different arguments; use a new one.
Finish or abort the interrupted materialization first.
Reconcile the uncertain push plan before publishing again.
The change is divergent; name one of its heads.
Resolve the conflicts first.
The cursor's view or lease expired; restart the query.
The prepared plan is stale; prepare a new one.
Fetch the missing objects, then retry.
A claim blocks the write until this instant.

GitCommitArgs.description:
`git.commit`: records one concrete commit with a caller-staged tree and
caller-supplied identities, plus one branch move applied atomically on
the lane. Unlike `new` (which mints an empty-tree change), every commit
input arrives stored and validated; the lane stages nothing but the
commit object itself.

A retried submission whose commit already landed and whose ref already
holds it skips the ref transaction, so the lane replays the stored reply
(same session, same request id) or succeeds idempotently instead of
failing its own compare-and-swap.

change_id.description:
Change to extend, when the caller resolved one. Absent keeps the
stable by-OID mapping, exactly like `ops::prepare_new` with no id.

predecessor.description:
The earlier head this commit rewrites for an amend-style rewrite.
`prepare_new` requires it to be a current head of `change_id`.

ref_update.description:
Branch move to apply atomically with the commit. Absent leaves refs
alone; detached-HEAD advances have no producer on this path.

GitCommitRefUpdate.description:
One branch move bundled with a `git.commit`: the ref, the target the
caller saw, and a `Set` to the created commit.

GitCompatWorkspace.description: A GitCompat workspace: real `HEAD`, index, and worktree, Git semantics.

HashKind.description: Repository object format. Fixed per repository; never mixed in one store.

HeadRef.description:
A GitCompat `HEAD`: a branch name or a detached commit.

A symbolic `HEAD` stores only the name. Whether it is born, and what it
resolves to, is read from the ref authority on demand ([`Self::resolve`]);
caching a second resolved OID beside the name would let the two disagree.
An unborn branch is simply a symbolic `HEAD` whose ref does not exist.

HeadRewrite.description: One change's head before and after a rewrite.

IdentityClaim.description:
An author or tagger identity a caller supplies. Both fields are refused
when they could break a commit header line.

IdentitySource.description: Where the identity recorded on a new commit came from.

oneOf.description:
The committer preserved from the rewritten commit: rewrites keep the
original signatures instead of synthesizing new ones.

IndexGeneration.description:
The per-workspace index generation. Every index mutation bumps it in the
same transaction as the rows; overflow fails instead of wrapping.

InlineBytes.description: At most 1 MiB once decoded; larger content is a staged object.

KeysetPage.description:
One stateless keyset page: rows plus the opaque position to resume
after. Unlike [`Page`], the cursor binds no 30-second lease: the caller
passes `next_after` back as the next request's `after`, so forge reads
never hold lease state for pagination.

next_after.description:
The last returned key as raw bytes: a ref name for `refs.list`, an
entry name for `tree`. Absent when the listing is exhausted.

KeysetPage2.description:
One stateless keyset page: rows plus the opaque position to resume
after. Unlike [`Page`], the cursor binds no 30-second lease: the caller
passes `next_after` back as the next request's `after`, so forge reads
never hold lease state for pagination.

next_after.description:
The last returned key as raw bytes: a ref name for `refs.list`, an
entry name for `tree`. Absent when the listing is exhausted.

LandExecuteArgs.description: `land.execute`: pushes the stored candidate bytes; never rebuilds one.

candidate.description:
The exact candidate the caller reviewed and attested; a mismatch with
the stored plan fails `E_STALE`.

LandLocalState.description: The local state after a remote landing.

oneOf.description: Local state was published.

The remote landed, but later local changes conflict with recording it.
The confirmed remote result is reported, not lost or retried.

LandPrepareArgs.description: `land.prepare`: freezes an exact candidate; it never moves a ref.

remote.description:
Where to push the landed candidate; absent means this store.
A present remote refuses: the transport push leg is not served yet.

target.description: The target ref to land onto, e.g. `refs/heads/main`.

base.description: The target tip the candidate was rebased onto.

candidate.description: The exact commit that will be pushed.

expires_at.description: Plans expire after one hour unless executed.

requirements.description: What must be signed for the candidate before `land.execute`.

MergeDriver.description: The driver that produced a path's merged content.

MergeMetadata.description:
The mode and grammar/adapter version that produced a merge result.

`language_set_version` starts at 1 and changes whenever grammar pins,
dispatch, composition, or structural merge rules change. The build-generated
manifest digest that accompanies it belongs to the policy-resolution tuple,
not to a result, and is not part of this record.

MergeMode.description:
The content-merge strategy resolved once per logical operation.

There is deliberately no third "auto" mode.

oneOf.description: Syntax-assisted three-way merging (the default).
Stock-Git content merging; bypasses every syntax adapter.

MergeNotice.description:
One structured merge notice, possibly coalescing many occurrences.

`path` is a byte-exact repository path. `region` and `detail` describe the
first (representative) occurrence; `occurrences` counts every coalesced
one and is at least 1.

MergeNotices.description:
The bounded notice set of one operation: the value of the native reply
field `merge_notices`.

Invariants (enforced at every construction and on deserialization):
at most [`MAX_NOTICES`] entries; entry keys `(path, language, code)` are
unique; the entries' occurrences sum to at most `total_occurrences`; and
`notices_truncated` is true exactly when occurrences were not retained.

MergeReport.description:
The metadata and notices that accompany one merge or mergeability result.

A Git-mode result carries no notices: explicit Git mode bypasses every
syntax and notebook adapter, so a notice there would misreport which
driver produced the bytes.

MergeSelection.description:
The merge driver choice for a logical operation. Absent resolves through
configuration to `syntax`; the effective mode and language-set version
come back on the reply, and one resolved mode applies to the whole
rewrite.

Merge_of_Nullable_FileTerm.description: Terms alternating +,-,+,...,+; always an odd number (>= 1). A single term is a resolved value.

Merge_of_Nullable_Oid.description: Terms alternating +,-,+,...,+; always an odd number (>= 1). A single term is a resolved value.

oneOf.description: Callable with or without a session.
Establishes a session; must not carry one.

Requires a session; never mutates (except an autosnapshot of a
workspace named in the request).
Requires a session; carries a request id and a receipt.

Dispatched before any coordinator call and gated by the daemon's
`admin_uids`; takes no session and no receipt.

identity.description: The identity recorded on any commit the operation created.

merge.description:
Effective merge mode, language-set version, and structured notices for
any operation that merged content.

operation.description:
The operation that recorded the mutation. Absent when no operation-tracked
state changed.

NativeWorkspace.description: A Native workspace: the current-change model, no index.

NewArgs.description:
`new`: creates one native change on the supplied parents (none is a root
change; conflicted and merge parents are allowed).

workspace.description: When present, the workspace switches to the new change.

NoticeCode.description: Why a merge produced a notice. The serialized spelling is the plan's.

NoticeInput.description: Which merge input a notice's byte range indexes into.

NoticeRegion.description:
A byte range inside one merge input.

Offsets index the input named by `input`, never a guessed output position.
The range is half-open: `start_byte..end_byte`.

Oid.description: Exact Git object id: lowercase hex, 40 characters (sha1) or 64 (sha256).

OpAttestationSubject.description:
One attestation an operation recorded: the attested kind and subject.
Recorded for lane (op-sourced) mutations from the operation's own
attestation rows, so proof lists read subjects without a stream walk.

after.description:
Ascending cursor: only operations strictly after this id, oldest
first. Absent keeps the newest-first walk.

page.description: Paging state; absent starts at the newest operation.

oldest_retained.description: The oldest operation still retained; older ones were pruned.

OpPruneArgs.description:
`op.prune`: applies the repository's retention policy; there is no
separate per-call policy.

OpRefDelta.description:
One ref moved by an operation: the ref name plus its before and after
targets. Recorded for lane (op-sourced) mutations from the operation's
own ref deltas, so orchestration readers need no stream walk.

attestation_subjects.description: Attested (kind, subject) pairs this operation recorded, deduplicated.

on_behalf_of.description: Provenance the invoking call declared; never an authorization input.

ref_deltas.description: Per-op ref deltas, in delta order within the operation.

undoes.description: The operation this one inverts, if it is an undo.

OperationId.description: A monotonic operation identity. The wire form is the bare integer.

Page.description: One page of rows and the cursor for the next one.

Binds a page cursor to the store, view, query, and lease it came from. A
server rejects a cursor whose binding differs from the request it
arrives with, and a cursor stops working when its lease expires.

PageLimit.description: Rows per page; above the maximum is rejected, not clamped.

PageRequest.description: The paging part of a read request.

cursor.description: Where the previous page stopped; absent starts at the beginning.

PathChangeKind.description: How a path differs from its parent.

PathPattern.description: Repository path pattern: literal segments, whole-segment `*`, and a trailing `**` (zero or more segments).

PathProvenance.description: Who wrote a path and how its content was merged.

oneOf.description: Every path.
These paths; each selects itself and everything below it.

PolicySetArgs.description: `policy.set`: replaces the landing policy of the repository.

Provenance.description:
Who created a commit: the authenticated session and the identity claims
the session's policy admitted when the commit was made.

The claims are a snapshot, so the commit stays attributable after the
session row has expired. Provenance is metadata stored beside the commit's
canonical bytes, never inside them: no claim becomes a Git header or part
of a `conflict-v1` frame.

ProvenanceClaims.description: Unverified claims: lowercase keys, string values without control characters.

PushArgs.description:
`push`: persists a `Prepared` plan, then sends. A crash after
transmission could have begun leaves the plan `Uncertain`.

PushAtomicity.description: Whether the remote applies the updates all-or-nothing.

PushReconcileArgs.description: `push.reconcile`: observes the remote's current refs for an uncertain plan.

PushRefStatus.description: The outcome of one pushed ref.

oneOf.description: The remote applied the update; `new` is absent for a deletion.

PushUpdate.description:
One remote ref update. Forcing a non-fast-forward still compares the
remote's advertised old value; `expected_old` absent means that advertised
value.

QueryArgs.description:
`query`: evaluates a revset to changes. An ambiguous prefix is an error
with candidates, never an arbitrary pick.

QueryDigest.description: SHA-256 digest of the canonical query: 64 lowercase hex characters.

heads.description: More than one head means the change is divergent.

ReadIntents.description: Access to other sessions' private provenance and claim details.

claims.description: May read other sessions' private claim details.

provenance.description: May read other sessions' private provenance claims.

onto.description: The new parents; at least one.

oneOf.description: Each source and all of its descendants.

Only the sources; their descendants are re-parented onto the sources'
old parents.

ReceiptRef.description:
The durable receipt of a mutation. A request that repeats an existing
`(session, request_id)` with the same digest is answered from the receipt
(`replayed`); a different digest fails `E_REQUEST_REUSED`.

retained_until.description: Receipts replay their original reply until this instant.

observed.description: The remote's current value; absent when the ref does not exist.

ReconcileVerdict.description: What observation found for one ref; observation is not causal proof.

ReconnectSecret.description: Session reconnect secret: 64 lowercase hex characters. Never logged.

RecoverAction.description: How to finish an interrupted materialization.

oneOf.description: Apply the remaining transitions to the recorded target.

Restore paths still matching the target or preimage; keep external
edits and report them as unresolved.
Explicitly overwrite these externally changed paths.

RecoverDisposition.description: What recovery did with one path.

RefConflictNote.description: A bookmark left unresolved by a three-way tracking merge.

RefExpect.description:
The value a caller expects a ref to hold before an update (compare and
swap). `Absent` is the wire's all-zero expected-old.

oneOf.description: No expectation.
The ref must not exist.

The ref must exist and hold exactly this target (compared unresolved:
a symbolic ref holds a name, not what it points at).

RefName.description: Full Git ref name under `refs/` (git check-ref-format rules). A JSON string when valid UTF-8, otherwise {"hex": lowercase hex}.

RefPattern.description: Full ref name pattern: literal segments, whole-segment `*`, and a trailing `**` (zero or more segments). Starts with `refs`.

RefTarget.description:
What a ref stores: an object id, or the name of another ref.

A direct target is never the null id and is not guaranteed to exist as an
object; objects are the store's concern. A symbolic target need not exist
either: that is an unborn branch.

RefsListArgs.description:
`refs.list`: ref names and targets with prefix and inclusive-start
seek. Covers single-ref resolve, so no separate `ref.get` exists.

after.description: Resume after this name; absent starts at `prefix` (inclusive).

prefix.description: Only names starting with these bytes; absent lists every ref.

as_of.description:
The event head the page was read under. Read before the page so it
never runs ahead of the events the page reflects.

ReleaseFreezeClearArgs.description:
`release.freeze.clear`: removes the released-tag marker of one tag when
the named release owns it. No marker is a no-op success; another owner is
refused.

ReleaseFreezeSetArgs.description:
`release.freeze.set`: writes the released-tag marker that freezes one tag
to a target for one release. A different owner, or the same owner at a
different target, is refused; the same owner at the same target is a
no-op success.

RemainingConflict.description: A path that is still conflicted after a resolution.

terms.description: Number of terms in the conflict (odd).

RemoteExpect.description: The remote value a push update is conditional on.

oneOf.description: The ref must not exist.
The ref must currently be this object.

RemoteName.description: Remote name: 1..=128 ASCII letters, digits, `.`, `_`, or `-`.

RemoteRefsArgs.description: `remote.refs`: advertised refs of an explicit remote URL, never stored.

RemoteSpec.description: A remote: a configured name or an explicit location.

RemoteUrl.description: Remote URL or local path: 1..=2048 bytes without control characters.

ReplyBody.description: A reply is a result or an error, never both.

request_id.description:
The request this answers, when the request was readable far enough to
have one.

RepoDeleteArgs.description: `repo.delete`: tombstones one repository; a purge job removes it.

RepoInitArgs.description: `repo.init`: creates one repository store under a configured root.

RepoPath.description: Repository-relative path bytes: `/`-separated, no empty, `.`, `..`, or `.git` component, no NUL. A JSON string when valid UTF-8, otherwise {"hex": lowercase hex}.

RepoRenameArgs.description:
`repo.rename`: moves one repository within its root; the store id is
unchanged.

RepoStatArgs.description:
`repo.stat`: store identity, object format, default branch, quarantine
latch, and the event horizon. Served from the store head; counts no
refs.

quarantined.description: Whether committed corruption latched quarantine in this session.

Request.description: A method call and its parameters.

RequestDigest.description: SHA-256 request digest: 64 lowercase hex characters.

session.description:
The authenticated session. Required by reads and mutations, optional
for `schema`, forbidden for `session.open` and `session.resume`.

Resolution.description: How one conflicted path is resolved.

oneOf.description: Explicit content.
Take one side: the zero-based index among the conflict's add terms.

Collapse sides that made the same change (the one opt-in lossy
collapse).

ResultingStamp.description: The workspace stamp a mutation produced.

RevertArgs.description: `revert`: a new change applying the reverse of `target`'s delta.

mainline.description: For a merge commit: the one-based parent whose side is kept.

onto.description: Parents of the new change; at least one.

RevisionRef.description: A tree to read: a commit, a change, or a workspace's working copy.

RevsetText.description: Revset expression text: 1..=65536 bytes without NUL.

RewriteReply.description:
The reply shared by methods that rewrite changes and re-derive their
descendants.

conflicted.description: Changes whose rewritten head is conflicted.

ScanExhaustion.description: Why a `search` page sealed before covering its tree.

oneOf.description: The page covers its tree; no budget ran out.
The byte or blob budget ran out at the sealed frontier.
The deadline passed at the sealed frontier.

SchemaArgs.description: `schema`: the versioned schemas of the protocol.

method.description: Restrict the document to one method; absent returns the whole model.

SchemaVersion.description: The schema version carried by every request and reply.

Scope.description:
Which part of the tree a workspace materializes. Out-of-scope trees stay
in the commit by id.

Cone semantics follow Git's: the root's files are always in; a listed
directory is in recursively; the files directly inside each ancestor of a
listed directory are in, its other subdirectories are not.

A scope change request is simply the new [`Scope`] value (set semantics);
the stamp fence on the workspace orders concurrent changes.

oneOf.description: No sparse checkout: everything is in scope.
Cone mode over the listed directories.

at.description: Head or change revision; a workspace revision refuses.

budget.description: Scan budget; absent fields take the defaults.

exclude_globs.description: Exclude globs; any match drops the path.

globs.description: Include globs; empty searches every selected path.

page.description: Rows wanted and the lease-bound continuation.

paths.description: Which tree paths the scan visits.

pattern.description: Byte-exact needle or regex over raw line bytes.

SearchBudget.description:
Scan budget of one `search` page: every field optional wire-wise, absent
means the default. Over-cap values refuse; they never clamp.

max_blobs.description: Unique blobs scanned before the page seals.

max_bytes_scanned.description: Decoded blob bytes scanned before the page seals.

SearchHit.description:
One matching line: 1-based line and byte-column numbers with the first
kibibyte of the line. Lines past the preview bound carry a trailing
`...` marker.

SearchPattern.description:
`search`: byte-exact or regex code search over one revision's tree,
served from the core-owned search pool with lease-bound cursors.

oneOf.description: Byte-exact needle; empty needles refuse.
Rust regex syntax over raw line bytes; empty patterns refuse.

SearchReply.description:
`search`: one path-ordered page of matching lines with lease-bound
continuation. `truncated` mirrors `hits.next.is_some()`; exhaustion
seals the page with a cursor instead of refusing.

SessionAuthority.description: What a resumed session may still do.

oneOf.description: Full authority until the idle expiry.
Write authority has expired; receipt lookup remains until the horizon.

SessionOpenArgs.description:
`session.open`: authenticates the caller's OS or service principal (the
request names no principal) and negotiates capabilities.

capabilities.description:
The subset wanted; absent asks for the principal's whole policy. A
request beyond the policy fails `E_FORBIDDEN`.

principal.description: The authenticated principal, as determined by the server.

Signature.description: An author or committer identity line.

email.description: Email bytes: no `<`, `>`, newline, or NUL.

name.description: Name bytes: no `<`, `>`, newline, or NUL.

timestamp.description: Unix seconds; negative values are pre-1970.

SignerFingerprint.description: SSH key fingerprint: `SHA256:` plus 43 base64 characters.

SnapshotArgs.description: `snapshot`: records the workspace's current content as its change.

SnapshotPolicy.description: Whether a workspace read snapshots first.

oneOf.description: Snapshot a native workspace before reading (the default).
Read without snapshotting (`--no-snapshot`).

changed_paths.description: Paths whose content differed; zero means no operation was recorded.

SplitArgs.description:
`split`: partitions one change into two. The unselected remainder keeps the
source change's identity; the selection becomes a new change.

paths.description: Must name paths; `all` would leave nothing to split.

SplitPlacement.description: Where the selected paths of a `split` go.

oneOf.description: The selected paths become a new parent of the remainder.
The selected paths become a new child of the remainder.

SquashArgs.description: `squash`: moves selected path changes from `source` into `destination`.

description.description: New description for the destination; absent keeps it.

keep_empty.description: Keep the source change even if it ends up empty.

StagedObject.description:
A reference to bytes uploaded ahead of the request that uses them. The
lease keeps the object alive until the request lands or the lease expires.

oid.description: Git blob identity of the staged bytes.

StatementDigest.description: SHA-256 digest of a canonical attestation payload: 64 lowercase hex characters.

applying.description:
A materialization is in progress: the directory is not a complete
snapshot.

snapshot_operation.description: The operation of the autosnapshot this read performed, if any.

StreamId.description: Correlates a reply with the raw data frames that carry its bulk bytes.

TagAnnotation.description: An annotated tag's message and optional tagger.

TagSetArgs.description:
`tag.set`: `name` is a full `refs/tags/` ref name. With an annotation the
tag is a real Git tag object.

target.description: The ref's new value (the tag object for an annotated tag).

TaskKey.description: Task key: 1..=128 bytes without control characters; the subject key renders as `task:<id>`.

Timestamp.description: RFC 3339 instant in UTC; the text ends in `Z`.

TreeArgs.description: `tree`: one directory listing with stateless keyset paging.

after.description: Resume after this entry name; absent starts at the beginning.

path.description: The directory to list; absent is the root.

size.description: Stored object length for blobs; absent for trees and gitlinks.

TzOffset.description: Git timezone offset: sign and four digits, e.g. +0100 or -0000.

UndoScope.description: Which operations `undo` may invert; ordered `Session < All`.

oneOf.description: Only operations performed by the same session.
Any operation.

UndoSummary.description: How many keys an undo restored.

ViewInfo.description: The store and operation snapshot a read was served from.

Warning.description: Something the caller should know that did not fail the operation.

oneOf.description: An advise-mode claim held by another session overlaps this write.

A snapshot of a published head started a new change instead of
rewriting the published one.
A push is uncertain, so this head is held as possibly published.

WorkspaceBinding.description:
A workspace and the stamp the caller believes it holds. The lease epoch is
checked before the sequence, so a fenced holder learns `E_LEASE_LOST`
rather than a misleading `E_STALE`.

WorkspaceInit.description:
The kind and starting point of a new workspace. The kind is fixed for the
workspace's lifetime.

oneOf.description:
A native workspace on a new current change over `parents`. No parents
is a root change.

A Git-compatible workspace with this HEAD (an unborn symbolic HEAD is
allowed).

WorkspaceStamp.description:
A workspace's compare-and-swap token.

`sequence` counts committed mutations of this workspace; `lease_epoch`
counts ownership takeovers. Unrelated workspaces have unrelated stamps.

WorkspaceState.description: A workspace of one fixed kind.

WriteArgs.description:
`write`: one atomic change from explicit edits. Inline content is at most
1 MiB per edit; larger content is staged and referenced. A path is never
split across edits.

WriteScope.description:
Which changes `write_changes` lets a session mutate; ordered
`Own < Session < All` (see the module docs for the interpretation).

oneOf.description: Only the change checked out in a workspace this session holds.
Additionally, any change this session created.
Any change.

WsDropArgs.description: `ws.drop`: unregisters the workspace; user files are never deleted.

scope.description: The cone scope; absent means the full tree.

WsScopeArgs.description: `ws.scope`: replaces the scope with the full new value.

WsTakeArgs.description: `ws.take`: fences the current holder by advancing the lease epoch.

expected.description:
When present the take only succeeds from exactly this stamp; absent
seizes the workspace from whoever holds it.
